newsitem.title: CANADA: SNC-Lavalin data depended on valid samples.
newsitem.headline: SNC-Lavalin data depended on valid samples.

text.p: SNC-Lavalin Group Inc said on Wednesday that the resource calculations it conducted for the Busang gold discovery were "prudent and reasonable," but that the estimates depended on the validity of the samples.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd earlier on Wednesday said tests of the Busang II and III areas of East Kalimantan, Indonesia appeared to have been overstated.

"The conclusions and recommendations provided in the various studies are believed to be prudent and reasonable and are founded on calculations and observations that were performed to accepted industry standards," SNC-Lavalin said.

SNC-Lavalin said the latest resource calculations showed that the gold resources at Busang, in all categories, were 889 million tonnes at an average grade of 2.48 grams gold per tonne for a total of 70.95 million ounces of gold.
But SNC-Lavalin said the scope of its mandate from Bre-X related only to resource studies and modelling.

"These calculations are dependent on the validity of samples and assaying of those samples. P.T. Kilborn Pakar Rekayasa (a unit of SNC-Lavalin) did not drill, did not take the samples nor did it assay those samples," the statement said.

Freeport McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc, a 15-percent partner in Busang, said on Wednesday an incomplete analyses of cores from seven holes it drilled in the Busang II area indicated "insignificant amounts of gold."

Bre-X said it has hired Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd., an independent Canadian mining industry consultant, to review Bre-X's technical programs at Busang and to review the due diligence being conducted by Freeport-McMoRan.
